patterns.what_worked: The guarantee to pin was an ABSENCE, so the mock had to become a witness: the ClearInspectPlayer mock now counts its calls in the two harnesses that actually drive an inspect (detect_test, tooltip_test) and stays a no-op to the client. Each pin carries a CONTROL (the inspected unit's data really landed in the cache) so a zero counter cannot pass because nothing happened. Both pins were proved red on a copy under /tmp/opencode, never in the tree.
patterns.what_was_hard: Choosing the resolution path for P2: the inspected unit must be neither target nor mouseover, or the fallback is not the thing under test. detect_test gives the unit its own token; tooltip_test has a shared UNITS model, so the token is added and removed inside the pin.
patterns.skill_gap: P3 was already covered by tooltip_test.lua, so a large part of the request was a report rather than an edit. The pre-existing state of the suite has to be READ before pins are written, not after.
